title: OEWD Program Director (Stabilization Fund)
statement:
**Cycle 117 weekly report — Marcus Webb, OEWD Program Director, West Oakland Stabilization Fund (INIT-001)**

**Where the money stands.** The Fund's authorization is $28 million. The tracker shows $20.2 million remaining this Cycle, down from $20.6 million at my last report — that $400,000 movement is the C114 tranche executing under the 23-day standard, and the tracker records Cycle 117 as the last disbursement cycle. The city's payments row for INIT-001, Cycle 117, carries no new entry. The four household grants I can name on the record — HH-0102-F027, HH-0109-F017, HH-0110-F019, HH-0113-F023, all West Oakland renters, last paid Cycles 109 through 113 — remain active with no flags. I'm still not quoting a cumulative number the sheet doesn't carry; the tranche lines are the authority.

**The queue.** Nothing new in the payments ledger this Cycle. And I won't dress it up: the tracker's "last disbursement" line and the payments line have drifted apart — one says 117, the other shows no 117 row — and that gap is exactly the kind of thing that turns a clean record into a contested one. My closing task from last cycle, getting the next authorization batch to the Deputy Mayor's desk, remains open. That's what I answer for.

**The charter renewal.** The tracker puts the next scheduled action — verify the C114 closeout, then Council charter-renewal consideration — at Cycle 118, not 117. So I'm correcting my own expectation from last week's report on the record: final action did not land this Cycle. What the row does hold: renewal support is contingent on the verified C114 closeout and Council action; the business-and-resident scope and the 23-day standard remain intact. The renewal vote fields are still blank and "Standing." The roll call belongs to the Council, and I won't call it before they do.

**The neighborhoods.** West Oakland reads housing pressure 6.5 this Cycle — up from 5.5 in my last report — with median rent $3,676 and median income $147,041, still on a growth trajectory. That rise in pressure is the whole argument for the queue not idling. I'm also noting on the record this Cycle's implementation effects: the Stabilization Fund and the Tenant Defense Fund both running as positive economic effects in West Oakland, set against the Youth Apprenticeship Pipeline sitting stalled — a negative sentiment and retail effect in this neighborhood, not somewhere else.

**What I'm watching.** Cycle 118: verify the closeout, get the authorization batch in front of the Deputy Mayor, and see the charter renewal to a vote with scope and the 23-day clock intact. And reconcile the disbursement line with the payments record before anyone else does it for me.
